req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must return HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter is missing or malformed. Examining the source code (lines 572-644), the handler does `response.headers["Location"] = args["url"].encode("utf-8")` — if 'url' is absent, a KeyError is raised (no explicit 400 guard exists in the shown source). This means the current implementation may raise a 500 rather than a clean 400, which is itself a defect the tests should expose. Tests cover: (1) positive — valid url param yields 302 with correct Location header; (2) negative — missing url param; (3) negative — empty string url; (4) boundary — status_code param at boundary values 300, 399, 400; (5) decision-table — custom 3xx status_code with valid url. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302_with_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=https://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'https://example.com'

tests.executable:

client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_location_header_exact_url_value():
    target = 'http://httpbin.org/get'
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=' + target)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == target
    assert r.headers['Location'] != ''
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/redirect/1'
